title: Deploy the Federation Hub as IaC
breadcrumb: Wire up Deploy App TAK Servers via a Federation Hub (IaC)
Deploy the Federation Hub as IaC

blocks.html:
The Federation Hub is not part of the stock Deploy App stack, so this is the new piece. It is still file- and CLI-driven, so none of it needs the UI. Bake each item into the image, volume, config-map, or secret that your pipeline manages.

The artifacts

The hub reads two YAML configs under /opt/tak/federation-hub/configs/:

  • federation-hub-broker.yml — federation and messaging: keystore/truststore names, the token-auth servers, optional MongoDB (for MFDT), and the policy the broker loads.
  • federation-hub-ui.yml — admin UI access, the authorized-users file location, and optional Keycloak OAuth for admin login.

Template both from your topology and secrets.

1. Certificate and trust

  • Hub identity: enroll the hub as a Deploy App product and get its server/client certs via RASENMAEHER sign_csr (or generate them with the bundled /opt/tak/federation-hub/certs scripts). Put them where the YAML expects them (takserver.jks keystore by default; set keyAlias to match).
  • Trust the servers: import each deployment's root_ca.pem into the hub's federation truststore (fed-truststore.jks by default). Your pipeline already has these PEMs (see the trust model).

2. Authorized admins

The hub authorizes admin identities from a file written by a CLI, which suits a one-shot pipeline job:

java -jar /opt/tak/federation-hub/jars/federation-hub-manager.jar \
  /opt/tak/federation-hub/certs/files/<admin>.pem
# writes /opt/tak/federation-hub/authorized_users.yml

Run it as an init/bootstrap container so authorized_users.yml exists before the UI service starts. You rarely need a human admin once the policy is templated, but authorize at least one cert for break-glass access.

3. Admin auth via Keycloak (optional)

Point the hub UI at the deployment's Keycloak so admin login uses Deploy App identity, in federation-hub-ui.yml:

allowOauth: true
oauthPort: 9099
keycloakClaimName: groups        # token attribute
keycloakAdminClaimValue: admin   # group that grants hub admin
# keycloakServerName / keycloakClientId / keycloakSecret / endpoints from your Keycloak

A user in the admin group can then administer the hub, with no separate hub credentials.

4. Token-auth port (optional)

If a link cannot do full mTLS (for example a network running break-and-inspect), enable a token-auth port in federation-hub-broker.yml:

federationTokenAuthServers:
  - type: jwt
    port: 9103

5. MongoDB for MFDT (optional)

For store-and-forward of mission/Data-Sync changes across disrupted links, run MongoDB and set its credentials in federation-hub-broker.yml.

Ports to expose

9100 (admin UI), 9102 (v2 federation, which servers connect to), and 9103 if you enabled token auth. Open them in the firewall or security groups via IaC.

The policy (which servers may talk, and what crosses) is the last artifact, covered next.
